payload.title: Close G9 spec-to-grammar conformance before parser freeze
payload.work_clay: On the Ubuntu FRANK v0.1 target, make the admitted ClayCode G9 V3 surface/spec parseable by the admitted grammar and parser without semantic escape hatches. Current concrete counterexamples include comparison operators used by the spec but absent from grammar (> < >=), conditional blocks used by the main cycle but absent from statement grammar, and receipt? or residual syntax not represented by current operator/primary rules. Prefer the smallest grammar/surface correction or canonical-spec rewrite that preserves existing semantics; do not redesign semantics unless an executable counterexample forces it.
payload.reason_clay: BASE_CLAYCODE_RELEASE is the first unpassed gate. The current G9 V3 spec and grammar are internally inconsistent, so CC-WP-01 SPEC-FREEZE and CC-WP-02 PARSER-CANON cannot truthfully close until a full spec->parser conformance test passes. Evidence refs: research_entity/claycode/g9/CLAYCODE_G9_FUSION_SPEC_V3.clay and research_entity/claycode/g9/grammar.ebnf.
payload.completion_clay: A repository test enumerates every admitted G9 V3 construct and parses the full current G9 V3 spec with zero unsupported syntax; parser->canonical IR->pretty/roundtrip preserves semantic hash; negative grammar tests reject malformed constructs; any semantic change is linked to a failing executable counterexample. Ubuntu test receipt and exact hashes are recorded.
payload.executor_policy: Research Entity local execution authority only. Prefer Claude/local repo build organ when capacity returns or another verified local executor. ChatGPT connector writes are coordination/research state, not proof that compiler/parser execution occurred.
invalidators: A newer admitted ClayCode stack pointer supersedes G9 V3 before execution
A verified existing parser receipt already proves full admitted-spec conformance
